title: Prelude in C major (BWV 846)
description: The opening prelude of The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I: one broken-chord pattern repeated through a chain of rich harmonies. A perfect study in even sixteenths, quiet hands and listening to harmony change under your fingers.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: The complete 35-bar prelude as Bach wrote it; the only editorial choice is notating the held tenor note as a sixteenth tied to a dotted quarter so every voice fills the bar.
teachingPoints: Learn the chord of each bar as a block first (bass, tenor, three right-hand notes), then unfold it into the sixteenth pattern.
Left hand: bass on the beat, tenor on the second sixteenth, both held while the right hand arpeggiates; keep the wrist loose and the dynamics even.
Hand-position shifts are marked at bars 1, 2, 5, 10, 16 and 19; the accidentals in bars 12, 14, 20, 22, 23 and 28 define the colour of each harmony.
Bars 33-34 break the pattern with a long right-hand arpeggio over the held low C; practice them slowly and let the final chord in bar 35 ring.
